complexity.correctness_reason: decode and encode recurse once per node, so any list longer than CPython's recursion limit (~1000 nodes) raises RecursionError — only the stated 100-node cap keeps every permitted input safe.
complexity.notes: Reported as O(n) under unit-cost arithmetic, but in digit-level terms decode/add/encode operate on n-digit numbers, so the true bit cost is higher than the per-digit carry pass of the previous submission — this is the real reason this version is slower in practice, and it also relies on CPython's arbitrary-precision ints rather than the node-wise structure of the problem. Both helpers recurse once per node, so recursion depth is O(n) (see correctness_reason). Style-wise, `encode` relies on an implicit `return None` for its base case, which works but is easy to misread; the `a+b` recomputation in the return line is a minor redundancy.
complexity.summary: Recursively decodes both lists into Python integers, adds them with built-in big-int addition, then recursively encodes the sum back into a linked list (with a special case for 0).
